correctness.rationale: In the language with named zero and ternary relational addition, every atomic two-pebble diagram is determined by the eight explicit equations. The exact rank-two EF criterion identifies the set of pointed one-step profiles. For each first-pebble x, at most eight exceptional choices of the second pebble occur; for all n >= 9, and separately n=7, a generic choice exists. All exceptional coincidences are determined by the element order truncated into 1, 2, 3, 4, >=5, parity, and whether x is divisible by two. Existence of these patterns in a cyclic group depends only on divisibility by 2, 3, 4, 8, hence gcd(n,24). Seven explicit rank-two sentences separate the seven exceptional orders and the eight stable gcd classes. The order-24 class proves optimality of the size-24 cyclic representative. The bundled checker exhaustively reproduces every atomic pattern through 64, the classification through 128, and explicit separators; it does not substitute for the infinite lemma.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Gomaa general depth bounds apply to the group class but do not determine the exact rank-two type partition; the two published prime-order refinements specialize to primes and do not classify composites. Broad EF tools alone require a separate computation of the exact atomic profiles.

The exact gcd(n,24) invariant beyond seven exceptions, explicit distinguishing formulas, and optimal 24-element cyclic bound answer quantitative depth/model-representative questions motivated by the archival group-depth literature; they are not merely a finite computed table or arbitrary narrow slice.
